analysis: The change to docs/developer/test.md is documentation-only. It updates the 'Last updated' stamp (line 3), rewords the CI runner statement at head lines 1243-1247 (runtime tests now run on 'macOS CI runners' with a pointer to build.md#ci-runner-routing), and rewords the darkbloom-route test description at lines 1807-1810. In that description, the test now pins each routed job's lanes (one per provider or cluster shard, matching the matrix), fallback, timeout and read-only permissions. It keeps release workflows on literal Blacksmith runners, and the macOS jobs of ci.yml are no longer stated as literal Blacksmith. No provider code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, cache, add-on hold or sandbox installer logic changes, so the threat-model entries (T-041, TB-011, TB-012, TB-013 and others) are not affected. The one security-adjacent aspect is the CI runner routing: ci.yml macOS jobs are now routed through a control plane instead of being literal Blacksmith. The visible diff shows only the documentation, not workflow changes, so I cannot tell whether routing was actually altered. Release and signing workflows remain documented as pinned to literal Blacksmith runners, so signing secrets exposure is not widened by this text. Integration should confirm that the real workflow and script changes (build.md, ci.yml, the test-darkbloom-route.py script) match this documentation, which is outside the supplied evidence. No concrete regression is identified here.
